name: protein kinase D1

function.text: PRKD1 encodes serine/threonine-protein kinase D1. Annotated molecular activities include kinase activity and diacylglycerol-dependent serine/threonine kinase activity. It participates in signal transduction and intracellular signal transduction.

germline.text: Strong or definitive GenCC assertions link constitutional variants to congenital heart defects and ectodermal dysplasia (autosomal dominant).

somatic.text: Reported somatic alteration contexts include Polymorphous adenocarcinoma; Cribriform adenocarcinoma of salivary gland. The alteration class and exact variant must be assessed in the disease context.

germline_associations.mechanism: Autosomal dominant; definitive GenCC assertion from G2P. Allele-specific mechanism requires review.

function.text: PRKD1 encodes serine/threonine-protein kinase D1. Based in part on similarity, it phosphorylates the epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) on dual threonine residues, which leads to the suppression of epidermal growth factor (EGF)-induced MAPK8/JNK1 activation and subsequent JUN phosphorylation. It phosphorylates RIN1, inducing RIN1 binding to 14-3-3 proteins YWHAB, YWHAE and YWHAZ and increased competition with RAF1 for binding to GTP-bound form of Ras proteins (NRAS, HRAS and KRAS). It acts downstream of the heterotrimeric G protein beta/gamma-subunit complex to maintain the structural integrity of the Golgi membranes, and is required for protein transport along the secretory pathway.

germline.text: Pathogenic germline variants are associated with congenital heart defects and ectodermal dysplasia (autosomal dominant).

somatic.text: Somatic alterations involving PRKD1 have been reported in polymorphous adenocarcinoma, cribriform adenocarcinoma of salivary gland, and colorectal adenocarcinoma.
